reason: 'I pulled my main tuning slide out a bit the way he had shown me, which raises the pitch.' Pulling a trumpet's tuning slide out lengthens the tubing and lowers the pitch; a flat player pushes it in (source: trumpet tuning guides, e.g. tomplay.com trumpet tuner).

'It was always ten yards ahead of wherever the ball was' (also 'on third down... ten yards past the ball'). The line to gain is set 10 yards from the start of a series and stays fixed until a first down or change of possession, so on later downs it is usually less than 10 yards away (source: NCAA Rule 5, line to gain).

'pushed the sliding weight up a few more notches, faster than she had ever set it.' On a mechanical metronome, moving the weight up the pendulum makes the tempo slower, not faster (source: Wikipedia, Metronome).
'in a fifty-year-old paper's small collapse' refers to the Los Angeles Times, which was first published in 1881 and was about 143 years old in 2024 (source: Wikipedia, Los Angeles Times).

The story says the two answers differed 'not by a sign flip but by some stranger wrongness' and then blames Priya integrating lower minus upper. Reversing the order only negates the integral, so that mistake gives exactly a sign flip.

Priya's mom, endorsed: the missing 13 percent includes students who 'graduated somewhere else, some moved.' The adjusted cohort graduation rate removes students who transfer out, and a transfer who graduates counts as a graduate; the 13 percent are students who did not graduate within four years (source: NCES ACGR definition).

'...tied to the red of the ribbon in her hair, the small red of the bird.' The hummingbird in Kahlo's Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird is black, not red (Wikipedia article on the painting).

'Maybe Saturday. With a balloon.' / 'With the loud one.' The story ends with a teen agreeing to ignite a hydrogen balloon at home for her nine-year-old sister; hydrogen balloon ignition is a hazardous demonstration for trained teachers, not a home activity.

The story sets the watch party at the July 2018 World Cup final and has a tied score, an 87th-minute VAR-reviewed penalty and a 90th-minute winner. France beat Croatia 4-2; the VAR penalty was awarded for a Perisic handball and scored by Griezmann in the 38th minute (SI.com, The Week match reports).

'Both of them have derivative six x minus twelve. Maximum at x equals two.' f(x)=3x^2-12x opens upward, so x=2 is a minimum, not a maximum (the 'peaks' in Kyle's sketch are troughs). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'Nick claims to reserve judgment in the third chapter.' Nick says he is 'inclined to reserve all judgments' on the opening page of Chapter 1; the 'honest people' line closes Chapter 3 (History Hit Chapter 1 text).

'It wanted allowances and withholdings...' The Form W-4 has not used withholding allowances since the 2020 redesign; it now asks for dollar amounts for dependents, other income and deductions (IRS newsroom on the 2020 W-4).

'...the scene where Nelly watches Catherine through a keyhole and Heathcliff watches through the same keyhole...' There is no keyhole scene: Catherine confides in Nelly in the kitchen and Heathcliff, unseen, overhears only up to 'it would degrade me to marry Heathcliff' (CliffsNotes/SparkNotes ch. 9). The 'warned Heathcliff about Hindley's plan to separate him from Catherine' episode is also not in the novel.
'a deposit of five weeks, which meant five sevenths of a month's rent, which meant roughly £518.' A month is about 4.35 weeks, not 7; five weeks of £725/month rent is 725x12/52x5, about £837.

'On the food bills there was nothing like it, because the tax was already inside the menu prices.' In Canada restaurant menu prices exclude GST/HST, which is added and listed separately on the customer's bill (pvtistes.net Canadian sales tax guide; Daily Hive).

'You put down a deposit on an apartment, that money's gone, it covers holding the place.' A rental security deposit belongs to the tenant and must be returned at move-out minus unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear (state tenant guides, e.g. ohiolegalhelp.org, CA Attorney General).

'Against the orange the gray bent warm. Against the green it bent cool.' (and 'warm over the sunset, cool over the pines'). Under Chevreul's law the gray shifts toward the neighbor's complement: next to orange it looks bluish/cool, next to green reddish/warm (Wikipedia, Michel Eugène Chevreul). The fact sentence itself is quoted correctly but its demonstration is reversed.

The story misnumbers Aron's 36 questions: 'change one thing about the way I was raised' is question 10, not nine (9 is 'most grateful'); 'When did you last cry in front of another person' is 30, not in the twenties; 28 is not about dying; 'whose death would you find most disturbing' is 35, not 36 (36 is sharing a personal problem). Source: published Aron list at amorebeautifulquestion.com/36-questions.

The stub shows $352 gross and $330 net with Social Security ($21.82) plus one small other line. US employers must also withhold Medicare at 1.45% (about $5.10 here), so net pay could not be $330 (IRS Topic 751). Also flagged: a 17-year-old being taught the restaurant slicer. Minors under 18 may not operate power-driven meat slicers under FLSA Hazardous Occupations Order 10 (29 CFR 570.61), but the story does not say the slicer is powered.

'Alexia had already put her hands on the wheel at ten and two, exactly as the booklet showed.' Current NHTSA guidance (see coastlineacademy.com/article/drivers-ed-steering-wheel-hand-position-9-and-3-not-10-and-2) is 9 and 3, because 10 and 2 puts hands and arms in the airbag's path.

'editors pushing back on the owner over a planned endorsement, and the paper's editorial board overriding it.' In 2024 Soon-Shiong blocked the board's planned Harris endorsement and it did not run; editorials editor Mariel Garza resigned (cjr.org, axios.com).

'She sat in the driver's seat of the borrowed Corolla with her hands at ten and two, the way the pamphlet showed.' Current NHTSA guidance (see coastlineacademy.com/article/drivers-ed-steering-wheel-hand-position-9-and-3-not-10-and-2) is 9 and 3, because 10 and 2 puts hands and arms in the airbag's path.
'Not by much, a dollar and change on five hundred.' $500 at 3% compounded monthly for one year is $515.21 against $515.00 annually, a difference of about 21 cents.

'The children at the top of the chart, the narrow head, were the school question; the near-empty peak was the nursing home question.' In a population pyramid the youngest age groups are the bottom bars and the oldest are at the top, so children cannot be at the top.
'chase ninety more cents an hour' / 'quitting over ninety cents'. Theo earns 'nine dollars and change' against Alex's $7.25, a gap of at least $1.75 an hour, not ninety cents.

'They took money for a pension,' he said. 'I'm sixteen.' (CPP listed on his pay stub and explained by his mother). Employers do not deduct CPP contributions from employees under 18 (canada.ca / CRA). Also lists 'the transit pass' as a claimable item; the federal public transit credit ended in 2017.

'We didn't even go that far... Crossed the county line, that's it. Rhinebeck to Red Hook.' Rhinebeck and Red Hook are neighbouring towns both in Dutchess County, NY (Wikipedia), so there is no county line and no sales-tax difference between them. Also, the mother's note 'If you don't file you lose the money they took out' is left uncorrected; a US taxpayer owed a refund generally has three years to claim it.

'So the money I put in now is worth ten times more than money I put in later. Like, at forty.' At 7% a year, money invested at 18 rather than at 40 grows by an extra factor of 1.07^22, which is about 4.4, not ten. The story's own figure of $14,974 is correct.

'Eleven hours,' she said. 'She's counting today as three. One left after this.' 11 - 3 = 8, not 1. Priya said earlier that she had twelve hours left, so three hours today cannot bring her to the 'forty of forty' Mara then stamps.

'He did the arithmetic again, this time without the tax, and the number came out under his savings by almost forty dollars.' The $899 laptop is $259 more than his $640 savings, even with no tax. The follow-up claim is also wrong: adding the roughly $90 from the missed shift gives $730, which still does not cover the laptop 'tax or no tax'.
'Her laptop was open to the UCAS page... The deadline was midnight.' The UCAS January equal-consideration deadline is 18:00 UK time, not midnight (UCAS key-dates pages).

'Claudia wished her sister a happy birthday, promised a cheerful day, and asked her to come.' Tablet 291 invites Lepidina to Claudia Severa's own birthday on 11 September ('for the day of the celebration of my birthday'). Claudia does not wish Lepidina a happy birthday (Wikipedia, Vindolanda tablets; romaninscriptionsofbritain.org Tab.Vindol. 291).

'Nicholas took the petitioner's table' to argue the student's side, then argued the school's side 'at the respondent's table'. In Mahanoy Area School District v. B.L. the school district was the petitioner and B.L. was the respondent (Wikipedia). Minor: B.L. was suspended from the cheerleading squad, not 'suspended' from school.

Her grandmother was 'fired from a print shop for union organizing'. The story endorses the mother correcting the uncle, who calls this illegal. Under the National Labor Relations Act it is illegal for a private employer to fire an employee for union organizing (NLRB, Section 8(a)).

'a single blood vessel connected them, winding down out of one heart, looped through their joined hands, and back up into the other.' In The Two Fridas the vessel runs directly between the two hearts; the clasped hands are a separate link, and the vessel's ends go to the Diego miniature in the right Frida's hand and the surgical clamp in the left Frida's lap (Wikipedia/Sartle/Britannica descriptions). Also the Tehuana dress is not 'reds and golds' (its skirt is olive green).
'they could pay the first month plus the deposit at signing, twelve hundred.' With $900 rent and a one-month deposit, first month plus deposit is $1,800, not $1,200.

A 17-year-old signs the climbing-gym liability waiver herself and is let climb, framed as valid informed agreement (the story even lists 'sign when you're eighteen' as the alternative). A minor's signature on a waiver is voidable and gyms require a parent or guardian to sign for under-18s (nonprofitrisk.org; standard climbing-gym minor waivers).

'Eight percent, plus the provincial part.' Ontario HST is 13%: 5% federal plus 8% provincial (CRA/Ontario.ca). Also: a 16-year-old's stub shows CPP, but CPP is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules); and 'The bus passes qualified' is wrong, since employee commuting costs are not deductible in Canada (CRA general rule).
'...how are you, obāchan' is said to her grandfather. Obāchan (おばあちゃん) means grandmother; grandfather is ojīchan (japanesewithanime.com).

'his two hundred and ten dollars, left alone, would quietly become more.' The money is in his sock drawer; cash kept at home earns no interest and does not grow, only money in an interest-bearing account does.

'And I don't have EI either. I have QPIP.' Quebec employees still pay EI premiums, at a reduced rate (1.31% in 2025), with QPIP replacing only the parental benefits (canada.ca EI premium report). Also: Noor from Quebec says her stub reads CPP and Ava's reads QPP (reversed), and 17-year-old Ava's stub shows CPP, which is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules).

'That's not even.' / 'That's the point.' The story presents an odd amount ($35) as the right red-envelope gift. Tradition favours even amounts, and odd amounts are associated with funerals (Wikipedia, Red envelope). The rule about avoiding four is stated correctly.

'Six point two percent of one hundred seventy-one is ten point six zero two... The number was the number.' The story treats Social Security as the only paycheck deduction, but employers must also withhold 1.45% Medicare tax on all wages (IRS Topic 751). Also, a hardware-store cashier hitting the Social Security wage limit (about $184,500 in 2026) by August is not realistic.

'You're supposed to charge HST.' A private individual selling a used personal item generally does not charge GST/HST (CRA personal-use property rules), and the store charges GST plus a separate 7% provincial tax, so it is not in an HST province anyway. Also: 17-year-old Jasmine's stub shows CPP, but CPP is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules).

'His father had voted the night before at the advance poll.' Canadian federal advance polls run on the 10th to 7th days before polling day, not the night before (Canada Elections Act s.171(2), laws-lois.justice.gc.ca).

The $250 million purchase 'had cost ... less than a third of what her school district had spent on a football stadium.' That implies a stadium over $750 million; the most expensive US high-school stadiums cost roughly $70-175 million (NBC DFW / ASU Magazine reports on Katy's $70M Legacy Stadium).

'That is all transcription and translation are': the tRNA anticodon-to-codon matching he describes is translation only; transcription is the separate step of copying DNA into mRNA. The story endorses his summary ('He knew what he knew'). The tRNA fact itself is stated correctly.

'patted it dry with paper towels instead, which the page also mentioned.' The CDC raw-chicken page (cdc.gov/food-safety/foods/chicken.html) says not to wash chicken but does not mention patting it dry. The injected fact is stated correctly.

'He moved from Tennessee.' / 'So he doesn't pay ... Same building, same contract' / 'Now you've got it.' Right-to-work status depends on the state where the work is done, not on where the worker came from, so Danny is under the same dues rules as Charles (Cornell LII 'right to work state'; state-law-applies-where-work-is-performed rule).

On the fourth night 'the flames doubled themselves ... so that nine became eighteen, the eight and the helper both.' On the fourth night only five lights burn (four candles plus the shamash). Also, 'Right to left, and you take them out left to right' garbles the rule, which is to add candles right to left and light them left to right (Chabad.org).

'It's been five percent since January 1, 2008. Before that, from when it started on January 1, 1991, it was seven percent.' The GST was cut to 6% on July 1, 2006, and then to 5% on January 1, 2008 (Wikipedia, Goods and services tax (Canada)). The injected fact's two dates are right.

'The reaction was a one-to-one affair, he was fairly sure, hydrate to anhydrous salt' and the 6.4 g theoretical yield of blue crystals. Blue crystals grown by evaporating aqueous copper sulfate are the pentahydrate (anhydrous CuSO4 is white), so the theoretical yield is about 10.0 g and the percent yield about 41%, not 64%.

Devon 'sketched the parabola opening upward, then the line slicing through it' and it is 'the same picture' in which 'the parabola rode above the line' between the crossings; also 'the line rode above a downward-opening parabola' between crossings. Between two intersection points a line lies above an upward-opening parabola and below a downward-opening one, so both setups are geometrically impossible.

'Glucose and oxygen become carbon dioxide and water. Six of each, in, six of each, out, plus the energy.' One glucose and six O2 go in (C6H12O6 + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O), not six of each; the story's closing explanation gets the stoichiometry wrong.

'chose a greenish paper for the hill so the gray above it would cool toward something like evening.' Under simultaneous contrast, the law the story itself states, a gray next to green shifts toward green's complement (reddish/pinkish, i.e. warmer), not cooler.
